sections.content: Now put the pieces together. A sentence about what you do and when can follow this order: time, how often, place or thing, verb. *Reggel mindig otthon reggelizem.* You do not need every slot: use the ones you need. The time can be a day (*hétfőn*), a part of the day (*reggel*), a month (*júniusban*) or *ebéd után*. *Nem* stands right before the verb; a frequency word comes after the time and before the place or thing. The verb ending shows who acts, so *én* stays out.

sections.title: Questions
sections.content: A question word also stands right in front of the verb, and the name goes after it: *Hol dolgozik Anna? Mikor főzöl? Hová mész?* There is no word for “do”.

items.english: In the morning I always have breakfast at home.
After lunch we walk in the park.
On Saturday evening I usually cook.
On Monday I am not going to school.

sections.content: English likes the verb early: “I always have breakfast at home in the morning.” Hungarian starts with the time and keeps the verb for later. Do not add *én*: *Reggel mindig otthon reggelizem* already says who.
